attempts.label: DANDI:000448
attempts.paper_title: Action spectra and mechanisms of (in) efficiency of bipolar electric pulses at electroporation
attempts.entry_title: Bipolar cancellation of electroporation and membrane charging kinetics (Kim et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's membrane charging results mostly held up, its results on how a second phase cancels electroporation held only in part, and its findings on pulse number, duration and repetition rate could not be tested, as those dishes are in other dandisets. Strobe imaging reproduced the mirror-image polarization of the cell poles, the bipolar overshoot and alternation, and summation without build-up, but not the fitted charging amplitude or discharge time constant, possibly because few of the paper's cells were deposited. Uptake rose with field and its inhibition was flat at high fields, but a 50% second phase left 49.3% of unipolar uptake, not about 20%. The exponential rise and weaker low-field inhibition held in part.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler and Pakhomov (2022) on dandisets 000489 and 000448. 000489 holds the stitched dish images of the Fig. 2 experiment, YO-PRO-1 uptake by BPAE monolayers after uni- and bipolar 600 ns pulses with second phases of 25 to 100%; 000448 holds strobe images of the membrane potential of 9 CHO cells during 833 kHz trains (Fig. 7). YP is measured in 200 um ROI along the bb' line with fields from a two-cylinder model, and pole traces are extracted from the strobe stacks. The experiments of Figs. 3 to 6 and the thermometry of Fig. 1E are not in either dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kim et al. (2022) from dandisets 000489 and 000448
Findings of attempt kim-2022-01 checked on 000489 version 0.230518.1811

outcomes.statement: For unipolar 600 ns pulses and for bipolar 600+600 ns pulses with every second phase amplitude, a train of 5 pulses at 1 Hz evoked YP uptake that increased with the local electric field strength.
outcomes.quote: A train of 5 pulses applied at 1 Hz evoked YP uptake proportionally to the local electric field strength ( Fig. 2A ), along with a strong dependence on the 2 nd phase amplitude.
outcomes.notes: With the two dishes that share one YP image left out (unipolar and 25% with 2 dishes, 50% with 5, 75% and 100% with 3), YP at the centre ROI (15.1 kV/cm) is higher than at the ROI 3 mm out (5.0 kV/cm) for all five amplitudes, unpaired p = 0.0001 to 0.044; Spearman rho of mean YP with field 0.96 to 0.99. The paired test passes for 3 of 5 (unipolar p = 0.12 and 25% p = 0.13, 2 dishes each). The weakest ROI at 2.4 mm and one-sided ROI give the same counts. Assigning the shared image to the unipolar or the 25% group gives 4 of 5 by the unpaired test.
deviations: Fields from an exact two-dimensional two-cylinder solution for the geometry of Methods 2.3 (15.38 kV/cm at the centre for 5.75 kV), scaled to the paper's 15.1 kV/cm there; the paper's finite element output is not deposited.

ROI are contiguous 200 um squares tiled from the midpoint along bb' to 3 mm on both sides, the claims file's reading (a), with the two ROI at the same distance averaged per dish; one side is shown as reading (b). The outer limit of 3 mm (5.0 kV/cm) is this attempt's choice, as the figure's field range is in the PDF only; 2.4 mm is shown as a variant.
YP0 and MB0 are means over a 0.2 mm disc at the centre of each footprint (Methods 2.5 says only within the electrodes' footprints); 0.1 and 0.3 mm discs are computed in the helper.
Pixel size 0.65 um, from the camera and objective named in Methods 2.5 (6.5 um pixels, 10x); the files give none. The measured electrode spacing (4.44 to 4.66 mm, Methods 4.5 mm) supports it.

Assumption. Methods 2.5 names a two-sided Student's t-test without saying whether it is paired. The unpaired test, the two-sample test the name denotes, is adopted; the paired result is shown. The readings differ here (5 against 3 of 5).
The dishes sub-Fig2-0-03 and sub-Fig2-25-04 share one YP image and are left out of the main analysis; both assignments are shown.

outcomes.statement: The vertical scale of the Fig. 2A panels goes from 1200 a.u. for unipolar pulses down to only 250 a.u. for bipolar pulses with a 75% second phase.
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 2A and its legend
outcomes.quote: note the difference in the vertical scale, which is varied from 1200 a.u. for unipolar pulses to only 250 a.u. for 75% bipolar pulses
outcomes.notes: The largest unipolar mean is 651 a.u. (mean plus s.e.m. 754, within 1200, and above 250). For 75% bipolar pulses the largest mean plus s.e.m. is 339 a.u. (311 to 372 over the readings), above the 250 a.u. axis; the largest 75% mean alone is 263 a.u. The unit-free ratio of the largest unipolar and 75% means is 2.47 (1.74 to 2.50 over the readings), against 4.8 for the paper's axes; axis limits only bound the data, so the ratio points the same way without deciding it.
deviations: The same ROI, field model and duplicate handling as fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

Assumption. The image values are taken as the paper's units (16-bit counts, conversion 1.0, footprint levels of 177 to 295 counts); the files are consistent with that but do not state it. If they were rescaled on export the criterion blocks the absolute values.

outcomes.statement: YP uptake increased exponentially with the field strength, and the second phase did not change the slope of the exponential fits on a semi-log scale.
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 2B and its legend
outcomes.quote: YP uptake increased exponentially with the electric field, and the presence of the 2nd phase did not change the apparent slope of exponential fits when plotted on a semi-log scale
outcomes.notes: Under the adopted reading (8 kV/cm cutoff, nonlinear least squares) an exponential fits the means with a lower residual sum of squares than a line for 3 of 5 amplitudes (unipolar and 50% are better fitted by a line; the criterion needs 4), and no bipolar slope from per-dish fits differs from the unipolar slopes (p = 0.12 to 0.80). The slope test has little power, as the unipolar group has 2 dishes (k = 0.205 and 0.41). Slopes of the fits to the means are 0.189 +- 0.016 (50%) and 0.191 +- 0.014 (75%) against 0.263 +- 0.027 for unipolar, 0.72 times; 25% and 100% give 0.88 and 1.07 times. The outcome changes with the reading. At 7 and 6 kV/cm with nonlinear fits the exponential is better for 4 and 5 of 5 and no slope differs (reproduced); with log-linear fits at 7 and 6 kV/cm all 4 bipolar slopes differ (p = 0.004 to 0.042, not reproduced) when the shared image is left out, and none when it is assigned to the unipolar group.
deviations: Fits by nonlinear least squares in scipy, not Grapher 16.

Assumption. The cutoff and the fitting method change the outcome. The criterion's main reading is adopted, 8 kV/cm (the top of the legend's "6-8 kV/cm", which leaves out the low-signal ROI of every amplitude) and nonlinear least squares on linear YP (the values the Fig. 2B legend plots); every variant is shown in the notebook.
The criterion does not say which outcome applies when the slopes agree but the exponential holds for fewer than four amplitudes; partially reproduced is used, as one of the two parts holds.

outcomes.statement: The strongest inhibition of YP uptake, to about 20% of the uptake after unipolar pulses, was reached with a second phase of 50 to 75% of the first (p < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2C and its legend
outcomes.quote: The maximum inhibition of YP uptake, down to ~20% of the unipolar pulses, was achieved with the 2 nd phase set to 50-75% of the first one (p<0.01, Fig. 2C ).
outcomes.notes: The ROI from 8.78 to 15.1 kV/cm (centre to 1.8 mm) are used. At all 10 the lower of the 50% and 75% values is below the 25% and 100% values. The best amplitude is 50%, at 49.3% of unipolar on average (reading a, recorded as measured) and 35.1% at its lowest (reading b), both outside 20 +- 2%. The p < 0.01 test does not hold at every field. Test (ii), the better of 50 or 75% against both 25 and 100%, gives p < 0.01 at 7 of 10 fields; test (i), against unipolar with 2 unipolar dishes, at 3 of 10; either at 7 of 10. No variant reaches every field (assigning the shared image, one side of the centre, footprint discs of 0.1 and 0.3 mm give 3 to 7 of 10 by either comparison). If holding at most fields sufficed, the outcome would be partially reproduced. Averaged over the 10 fields the 25% and 100% pulses give 110.0% and 118.1% of the unipolar value (64 to 168% at single fields), so on average they do not inhibit in these dishes; 25% is below 100% at 7 of 10 fields. The 75% and 100% dishes were imaged on 2021-08-24 and the two unipolar dishes analysed on 2021-07-29, with footprint YP0 of 177 to 227 a.u. against 236 and 292 a.u.
deviations: Assumption. The criterion runs the test at each field and does not say at how many fields it must hold. It is taken to hold, like the ordering, at every field in the range; round 1 had counted it as holding at most fields, a rule with no basis in the criterion or the paper.

outcomes.statement: Between 8.7 and 15.1 kV/cm the degree of inhibition by the second phase did not depend on the field strength.
outcomes.quote: The degree of inhibition showed no dependence on the electric field strength between 8.7 and 15.1 kV/cm.
outcomes.notes: Percent of the unipolar mean at 8.78 against 15.1 kV/cm, unpaired, ROI on both sides; 25% 103.8 against 97.7 (p = 0.83), 50% 67.8 against 35.1 (p = 0.072), 75% 91.5 against 40.0 (p = 0.15), 100% 121.3 against 114.6 (p = 0.78). The 50% and 75% differences are large (+32.7 and +51.5 points) with 5 and 3 dishes, so the absence rests on few dishes, not small effects. Paired p = 0.11 to 0.89. Assigning the shared image and footprint discs of 0.1 and 0.3 mm also give 0 of 4. With one side of the centre only one amplitude differs, 100% under (b+) (p = 0.033) and 50% under (b-) (p = 0.036), which would make it not reproduced. Over every pair of ROI in the range 19 of 180 comparisons differ at p < 0.05, against 9 expected by chance.
deviations: Assumption. The ROI placement changes the outcome. Reading (a), the ROI on both sides of the centre averaged per dish, is adopted, as bb' runs from b to b' through the centre (Fig. 1C) and the two halves have the same fields; one side only is shown.

outcomes.statement: Inhibition was weaker at 6.7 kV/cm than at the higher field strengths, with p < 0.01 for the 50% bipolar pulses and p < 0.05 for the 100% bipolar pulses.
outcomes.quote: However, inhibition was weaker at 6.7 kV/cm (p<0.01 compared to the higher electric field strengths for 50% bipolar pulses, and p<0.05 for 100% bipolar pulses).

statistics.about: 50% bipolar, 6.7 kV/cm against higher field strengths
100% bipolar, 6.7 kV/cm against higher field strengths

outcomes.notes: At the ROI closest to 6.7 kV/cm (2.4 mm, 6.63 kV/cm) 50% pulses give 198% of the unipolar mean, against 35 to 68% at 8.78 to 15.1 kV/cm, and 100% pulses 283% against 93 to 139%, so the percent is higher than at every higher field for both. Unpaired, 100% differs from each higher field with p <= 0.022 and from the per-dish pooled value with p = 0.011; 50% does not reach p < 0.01 (p up to 0.082 against each field, 0.049 against the per-dish pooled value). Paired gives the same (50% pooled p = 0.070, 100% p <= 0.035). The criterion as written pools the dish values of all higher field ROI; taken literally, every dish and ROI value pooled, it gives 50% p = 1.5e-09 and 100% p = 2.6e-09, and the outcome would be reproduced, under every variant shown. That pooling counts each dish ten times, so the per-dish mean is used (a deviation from the criterion's letter) and the outcome is partially reproduced. With one side of the centre, (b+) gives the same outcome and (b-) passes neither amplitude (100% pooled p = 0.078). The percentages above 100% mean more uptake than after unipolar pulses, not weaker inhibition in the paper's sense; the unipolar mean at 2.4 mm is 19 a.u. (dishes 25 and 12), near background and smaller than the spread of background between dishes (raw YP far from the electrodes minus YP0, -7 to 127 a.u.). The 100% pass rests on this ratio to a near-background mean from 2 dishes; the criterion counts it, and it is counted here.
deviations: Assumption. The unpaired test is adopted, as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field; the paired result is shown.

Pooled reading (ii) is taken per dish, each dish's mean percent over the higher field ROI, so that the test counts dishes; round 1 pooled every dish and ROI value, which treats the ROI of a dish as independent. This departs from the criterion's wording ("the dish values of all higher field ROI pooled"), under which the outcome would be reproduced.
Assumption. ROI reading (a), both sides of the centre, as for fig2c-inhibition-flat-above-8-7; one side only is shown.

outcomes.statement: Unipolar 600 ns pulses depolarized the membrane quickly at the cathode-facing pole of the cell and hyperpolarized it in mirror image at the anode-facing pole.
outcomes.quote: Unipolar nsEP caused fast membrane depolarization at the cathode-facing pole of the cell, and a mirroring hyperpolarization at the anode-facing pole.
outcomes.notes: Over 5 unipolar cells, at 600 ns the cathode-facing pole is +22.1% (p = 0.0012) and the anode-facing pole -20.7% (p = 0.0026), ratio of magnitudes 0.94; the 500 to 600 ns mean gives +22.1 and -21.4%. Five variants of the pole regions give ratios 0.90 to 1.05, all p <= 0.013, among them regions that leave out membrane facing a neighbouring cell (+22.1 and -20.4%, ratio 0.92). In all 9 cells the upper pole of the image rises and the lower falls during the first pulse.
deviations: 5 of the paper's 18 unipolar cells are in the dandiset.

Assumption. The paper does not say how the pole regions were drawn. They are the membrane pixels (frame-averaged image above its 85th percentile, largest connected group) where the outward normal of the smoothed cell outline is within 45 degrees of the image's vertical axis, the axis of the response in every file; 80th and 90th percentiles and 30 and 60 degrees are variants. Images are binned 2 x 2 on loading. The paper imaged individual cells or small groups (Methods 2.6); where the group is several touching cells, the regions include some membrane at cell contacts and notches that faces a neighbouring cell. A variant keeps only pole pixels with no other part of the group beyond them along the field axis (61 to 100% of the pole pixels per file).

Assumption. The files do not say where the electrodes were. The pole that brightens is taken as the cathode-facing one, as FluoVolt emission rises with depolarization and the cathode-facing pole depolarizes (Results 3.5). This makes the sign of the cathodic change a premise; the test is that the opposite pole changes the other way by a similar amount.

The pulse onset is not in the files; it is the first forward-trial frame where the mean unipolar upper-minus-lower signal exceeds its baseline by 5 SD (frame 43). The baseline is the 40 frames before it (Methods 2.6). Dark frames (failed flashes) are left out. Reverse trials are reversed and aligned to the forward trial by correlation (a lag of 74 frames in 8 cells and 75 in cell24) before the two are averaged (Methods 2.6).

outcomes.statement: Fitting the cathodic pole response to the first unipolar pulse gave a charging time constant of 200 ns and a maximum polarization of 31% emission change (425 points, r = 0.93, p < 0.0001), and the discharge after it a time constant of 520 ns from 31.5% (425 points, r = 0.85, p < 0.0001).
outcomes.source: Results 3.5, paragraph 2; Figure 7 (dotted lines, top panel) and legend
outcomes.quote: The best fit for membrane charging with an exponential function (using the first pulse in the unipolar pulse train) yielded the time constant of 200 ns and the maximum membrane polarization at 31% emission change (425 datapoints, correlation coefficient 0.93, p<0.0001). The best fit for the discharging portion of the curve yielded the same initial polarization (31.5% emission change) but, unexpectedly, a 2.5 times larger time constant of 520 ns (425 datapoints, correlation coefficient 0.85, p<0.0001
outcomes.notes: Over 5 unipolar cells, pooled points (125 for the charging fit over 0 to 600 ns, 120 for the discharge over 600 to 1175 ns), the charging fit gives tau = 191 ns (within 200 +- 20) and A = 23.2% (expected 31 +- 3.1); the discharge fit tau = 613 ns (expected 520 +- 52) from 22.7% (expected 31.5 +- 3.15). r = 0.84 and 0.64, p < 1e-14; the mean trace gives the same parameters with r = 0.998 and 0.997 and residuals of at most 1.4 points. Discharge over charge is 3.2, against 2.5. The charging tau is not robust to the onset, which is known to a frame; moving it by one frame gives 149 to 249 ns, and placing t = 0 half a frame earlier 216 ns. The discharge tau (615 to 627 ns) and both amplitudes (21.9 to 24.7%) stay outside tolerance in every case. Per cell, A ranges from 14.4 to 31.3% and discharge tau from 351 to 833 ns, so the subset of 5 cells of 18, and the assumed pole regions, may explain the difference. Leaving out the pole membrane that faces a neighbouring cell gives the same fit (A = 23.2 and 22.8%, tau = 191 and 614 ns).
deviations: 5 of 18 cells, so 120 points per fit where the paper has 425.
Pole regions, cathode side and onset as in fig7-unipolar-pole-polarization (assumptions).
Fits by nonlinear least squares in scipy, not Grapher 16; r is the correlation of the points with the fit.

outcomes.statement: Fits to the later pulses of the unipolar train gave the same kind of difference between charging and discharging time constants as the first pulse.
outcomes.quote: Fitting the membrane potential for the next pulses in the train consistently produced similar differences between the charging and discharging time constants (data not shown).
outcomes.notes: With the criterion's A(1 - exp(-t/tau)) form, discharge over charge is 7.9, 10.5, 8.9 and 9.1 for pulses 2 to 5, so the discharge constant is the larger for all four, but no ratio is within 2.25 to 2.75 or within 10% of the first pulse's 3.22 (2.90 to 3.54). That form cannot follow a pulse that starts from a charged membrane (charging tau 62 to 80 ns). With the free-start variant the ratios are 2.99, 3.62, 2.88 and 2.97, the discharge constant again the larger for all four; none is within 2.25 to 2.75 and pulses 2 and 5 are within 10% of the first pulse's ratio (pulse 4 just below). Both forms give partially reproduced.
deviations: The free-start charging fit, V0 + (A - V0)(1 - exp(-t/tau)), is a variant added here, as Results 3.5 says charging by later pulses "started with the partially charged membrane"; the criterion's form is the main one.
Pole regions, cathode side and onset as in fig7-unipolar-pole-polarization (assumptions).

outcomes.statement: Bipolar pulses caused the same initial polarization as unipolar ones during the first phase, followed by a faster discharge and an overshoot into the opposite polarity.
outcomes.quote: Bipolar nsEP caused the same initial polarization during the first phase of the pulse, followed by a faster discharge and an overshoot into the opposite polarity.
outcomes.notes: (i) At 600 ns the cathodic pole is 21.5% for 4 bipolar and 22.1% for 5 unipolar cells, unpaired p = 0.855; the error-bar gap rule finds no difference. (ii) After the first phase the bipolar mean falls to half in 150 ns (unipolar 475 ns) and to zero in 325 ns (unipolar not within 600 ns). (iii) The bipolar mean reaches -8.1% at 1175 ns; cell values -6.7 to -9.9%, p = 0.0012. That time was chosen on the mean of the same cells; the last frame of the second phase, fixed in advance, is the same frame.
deviations: 4 of the paper's 17 bipolar cells and 5 of its 18 unipolar cells.
Pole regions, cathode side and onset as in fig7-unipolar-pole-polarization (assumptions).

outcomes.statement: In 833 kHz trains, bipolar pulses caused the membrane potential to alternate repeatedly between positive and negative values.
outcomes.quote: Bipolar pulses caused repetitive alternation between positive and negative membrane potentials, which could facilitate pore closure beyond just returning the potential to the base level.
outcomes.notes: For each of the five pulses, over 4 bipolar cells, the cathodic pole is positive at the end of the first phase (19.3 to 21.5%, p <= 0.0001) and negative at the second-phase minimum of the mean (-8.1 to -9.1%, at 1150 to 1175 ns, p <= 0.0013). The value at 1175 ns of each period, a time fixed in advance, gives -8.1 to -9.1% with p <= 0.0017.
deviations: 4 of 17 cells; pole regions, cathode side and onset as in fig7-unipolar-pole-polarization (assumptions).

outcomes.statement: With 600 ns unipolar pulses at 833 kHz, each pulse charged the membrane to the same peak, with no stepwise build-up; the pulses merged into a continuous sawtooth polarization.
outcomes.quote: Although charging by the subsequent pulses in unipolar pulse trains started with the partially charged membrane, it reached the same peak potential. A stepwise build-up of the peak membrane potential ... did not occur in our experiments with 833-kHz, 600-ns unipolar pulses.
outcomes.notes: Over 5 unipolar cells, the peaks at the end of pulses 2 to 5 (23.4 to 24.3%) do not differ from the first (22.1%) by the unpaired test (p = 0.61 to 0.75), and the trace before each of pulses 2 to 5 stays above rest (8.8 to 9.9%, p = 0.009 to 0.017). The paired variant finds pulses 2 to 4 1.7 to 2.2 points higher (p = 0.014 to 0.040), a build-up of 7.8 to 10.1% of the first peak within cells; pulse 5 is 1.4 points (6.1%) higher, p = 0.089. The maximum within each pulse gives the same picture (unpaired p = 0.72 to 0.78). With 5 cells the absence found by the unpaired test, the test the criterion names, is weak evidence.
deviations: 5 of 18 cells; pole regions, cathode side and onset as in fig7-unipolar-pole-polarization (assumptions).

outcomes.statement: Uptake rose with field strength and with pulse number for both uni- and bipolar pulses, almost linearly with the number of pulses, so that plots for 5, 10 and 15 pulses look alike when the y-axis is scaled to 800, 1600 and 2400 a.u.
outcomes.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3A to C and legend
outcomes.quote: Increasing the pulse number increased YP uptake almost linearly [ 15 ]. Therefore, YP uptake plots for 5, 10, and 15 pulses appeared almost identical when plotted with the y-axis scaled proportionally (to 800, 1600, and 2400 a.u., respectively).
outcomes.notes: The dishes given 5, 10 or 15 pulses (Fig. 3) are not in 000489 or 000448, the datasets the claims file names. Dandiset 000548, which names this paper and whose title and description match dishes given 5, 10 or 15 pulses (Fig. 3), likely holds them; it is not among the paper's datasets in papers/datasets/kim-2022.yaml and was not used (listed under missing_datasets).

outcomes.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 3D and its legend

outcomes.statement: Bipolar 600+600 ns pulse trains at all kHz rates were less efficient than at 1 Hz, barely above background, the difference being largest (2.5 times) at the highest field.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, the efficiency of bipolar pulses at all kHz frequencies was less than at 1 Hz, and the electroporative uptake of YP was just marginally above the background level ( Fig. 6B , E ). The difference between 1 Hz and kHz-rate trains was maximum (2.5 times) at the highest electric field strength.

outcomes.quote: For high-frequency nsEP bursts, stronger electric field enhanced cancellation ( Fig. 6C , F ).

outcomes.statement: In the worst case tested, trains of 5 bipolar pulses (second phase 50%) at 1 Hz heated the sample to no more than 30 degrees C; at 833 kHz heating exceeded 30 degrees C but never reached 44 degrees C, and stayed close to 30 degrees C along the bb' line.
outcomes.quote: Pulses applied at 1 Hz (the repetition rate used in all but one sets of experiments) caused only modest heating, not exceeding 30 °C. At a high repetition rate of 833 kHz, heating exceeded 30 °C but never reached the next transition point of 44 °C and remained close to 30 °C (green to blue transition) along the bb' line
outcomes.notes: The thermochromic sheet photographs are not in either dandiset. 000489's Fig1F file is a sample of the cell staining (Fig. 1F), not thermometry. The titles and descriptions of the other dandisets that name this paper (000548, 000549, 000550) do not mention thermometry; their files were not opened.

findings.statement: 000489 holds only the 17 dishes of Fig. 2 and one sample image (Fig. 1F); 000448 holds the strobe images of Fig. 7. The dishes of Figs. 3 to 6 and the thermometry of Fig. 1E are in neither. Three more dandisets of the same lab name the paper in their metadata and match Figs. 3, 4 and 6 by title (000548, 000549, 000550); the registry's list of the paper's datasets and the 000489 title, which the claims file follows, do not point to them, so their 12 claims are blocked here and the thermometry claim is blocked as missing.
000448 holds 5 unipolar and 4 bipolar cells, where the paper reports 18 and 17. The dandiset does not say how the 9 were chosen.

The YO-PRO-1 channel (index 1) of sub-Fig2-0-03 (unipolar) and sub-Fig2-25-04 (25% bipolar) is the same image, value for value, while their MemBrite channels differ. One recording was deposited under two dishes of different conditions, and nothing says which dish it belongs to; the two files also give different session dates (2021-07-29 and 2021-07-26). With it left out the unipolar and 25% groups have 2 dishes each.
The two channels of the 000489 sample image sub-Fig1F (MemBrite and YO-PRO-1 by its session description) are the same image, value for value.

The 000489 images give no pixel size (resolution -1), no electrode positions or polarity, and no ROI positions or values; the analysis has to locate the footprints and assume 0.65 um per pixel, which the electrode spacing supports. The field of each ROI, from the paper's finite element model, is not deposited.

The series description of the 17 Fig. 2 files of 000489 names "Channel1" for both filter sets and for MemBrite; the data show index 0 is MemBrite and index 1 YO-PRO-1. It also describes 144 images (12 x 12) of a well of a six-well plate, where Methods 2.5 describes 216 images of 35 mm dishes. Three files name their series "Fig2_25" without the dish number.

The 000448 files give no pole regions, no field direction relative to the image, and no delay of each frame or frame of the pulse onset. Reverse-trial files store frames in acquisition order (descending delay), and their response is offset by 74 frames (1.85 us) from the forward trial of the same cell (75 frames for cell24); neither is documented.
000448 counts 18 subjects, but each cell is two files (forward and reverse trial) with different subject ids (for example 001_F and 001_R for cell09), so it holds 9 cells.

In 000448 the darkest frame of 10 of the 18 files is the first. Frames below half the file's median frame mean (about 180 counts against medians of 300 to 500) occur in 5 files, at frame 0 in 4 and at other frames in 3, consistent with failed laser flashes.

Question for the authors. How were the ROI placed along bb' (number, spacing, and whether both sides of the centre were used), and was the t-test paired when ROI of the same dishes were compared? This attempt tiled contiguous 200 um ROI from the centre to 3 mm on both sides and used the unpaired test; the paired test changes fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field from 5 to 3 of 5 amplitudes, and using one side of the centre changes fig2c-inhibition-flat-above-8-7 and fig2c-weaker-at-6-7.

Question for the authors. How were the cathode- and anode-facing pole regions drawn in the strobe images, and where was the cathode relative to the image? This attempt took the membrane within 45 degrees of the vertical axis and the brightening pole as cathodic. The charging amplitude found (23% against 31%) may depend on the regions; leaving out membrane that faces a neighbouring cell in the groups of touching cells does not change it. Were the poles of a group taken on the group's outline or on each cell?

Each of the 18 files of 000489 stores its stitched two-channel image as one ImageSeries with data of shape (22323, 22323, 2), a starting_time rate of 2.0 Hz and unit n.a. An ImageSeries takes the first axis as time, so each file reads as 22323 frames of 22323 x 2 pixels; two GrayscaleImage objects in an Images container, or a series of shape (1, 22323, 22323) per channel, would describe the data. The three 25% files share the acquisition name Fig2_25.

The dish numbers in the subject ids of the 000489 Fig. 2 files run up to 18 (Fig2_50_18), while 17 dishes are deposited (3 per amplitude, 5 at 50%), and neither the dandiset description nor the files say which dishes were exposed, which were left out, or why. All unipolar dishes have the session date 2021-07-29 and all 75% and 100% dishes 2021-08-24, a date with no unipolar dish. Measured along bb', the 100% dishes take up more YP than the unipolar ones (largest mean 750.5 against 650.8 a.u.; higher at 9 of 11 ROI within 2 mm of the centre), where Fig. 2C shows every second phase inhibiting uptake.

outcomes.note: A change in the claims file. The earlier file required the paired and unpaired tests to agree and the earlier attempt found 3 of 5 amplitudes under both; the current file judges the unpaired test, which passes for 5 of 5 here. Differences in method also move the unipolar and 25% unpaired tests below 0.05 (earlier p 0.11 and 0.15); YP0 and MB0 come from 0.2 mm discs here against 0.5 mm discs, the 25% group has 2 dishes against 3, and the field is scaled to 15.1 kV/cm at the centre. The paired test passes for 3 of 5 in both.

A change in the claims file. The earlier file ran 12 readings and the earlier attempt found none meeting both parts; the current file fixes one reading (8 kV/cm, nonlinear least squares, per-dish slopes), under which no slope differs and the exponential is better for 3 of 5. The two attempts also map this case differently, the earlier to not reproduced and the blind one to partially reproduced, as one part holds. The ROI method differences of fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field apply too.

A difference in method. The earlier attempt found 50% and 75% differing under both tests (unpaired p 0.0016 and 0.018), so the claims file's move to the unpaired test does not explain it. The high field ROI is the centre ROI here and the ROI 0.2 mm out (15.24 kV/cm) there, and the smaller footprint discs for YP0 and MB0 raise the unipolar mean at the low end of the range (87.9 a.u. at 1.8 mm in earlier_findings.ipynb, against 47.7 a.u. at 8.94 kV/cm), which lowers the bipolar percentages there.

A difference in method. The earlier attempt blocked the claim because the unipolar mean at 6.75 kV/cm was -8.6 a.u., at background by its rule of twice the s.e.m.; with 0.2 mm footprint discs the unipolar mean at 2.4 mm is 19 a.u. here, and the blind attempt applies no background rule. The earlier attempt's variants with smaller background (left footprint, bottom side) also gave a testable claim.

A change in the protocol. Under pilot-12 the earlier attempt tested 000489 alone and blocked the Fig. 7 claims as resting on 000448; under pilot-14 the paper's datasets include 000448, which the blind attempt used.
A change in the protocol, as for fig7-charging-time-constant; the data are in 000448, which the earlier attempt did not use.

disagreements.reason: Primary reading (8 kV/cm cutoff, NLS), the exponential beats a straight line for only 3/5 amplitudes, below the required 4, while 0/4 bipolar slopes differ from unipolar. The outcome flips with the reading; at 6 or 7 kV/cm with NLS it is reproduced, and with log-linear fits at 6 or 7 kV/cm 4/4 slopes differ. The notebook neither adopts a reading with a reason nor blocks the claim. The per-dish slope t-test has almost no power because unipolar has n=2, and the slopes of the fits to the means for 50% and 75% are 0.72x unipolar.

100% passes on a valid test (per-ROI unpaired, max p=0.0215). 50% reaches p<0.01 only through the pooled unpaired test (p=1.5e-9), which treats 50 ROI values from 5 dishes as independent; its valid tests give per-ROI max p of 0.08 to 0.10 and a pooled paired p of 0.07. The cell also ORs together the paired and unpaired variants. The low-field percents are not meaningful, as the unipolar denominator rests on n=2 dishes near background, giving 198% and 283% of unipolar, which is bipolar uptake above unipolar, not weaker inhibition.

entries.name: kim-2022
entries.title: Bipolar cancellation of electroporation and membrane charging kinetics (Kim et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler and Pakhomov (2022) on dandisets 000489 and 000448. 000489 holds the stitched dish images of the Fig. 2 experiment, YO-PRO-1 uptake by BPAE monolayers after uni- and bipolar 600 ns pulses with second phases of 25 to 100%; 000448 holds strobe images of the membrane potential of 9 CHO cells during 833 kHz trains (Fig. 7). YP is measured in 200 um ROI along the bb' line with fields from a two-cylinder model, and pole traces are extracted from the strobe stacks. The experiments of Figs. 3 to 6 and the thermometry of Fig. 1E are not in either dandiset.
